# ARIA — Copilot assistance

Read docs/ARIA-MASTER-HANDOFF.md first. It is the only current project-state document; follow NEXT STEP ORDER. Archived material is evidence, not a competing roadmap.

Codex is the primary author and integration reviewer. Help with bounded implementation drafts, meaningful test cases, targeted review and concise code explanations. Work only on explicitly assigned files and acceptance criteria. Return a short diff summary, checks performed and unresolved assumptions; avoid repeating the whole repository.

Preserve captured source and last-known-good evidence. Do not invent hardware pinmaps, I2C addresses, tuning, firmware identity or test results. Do not change frozen PRD, pinmap, motor tuning or safety behavior without an explicit scoped assignment and primary review. Never flash hardware, run motors, SSH to devices, push, merge or publish as part of a helper assignment unless separately authorized.

Separate VERIFIED (static/source), owner-reported evidence, PARTIALLY VERIFIED and NOT VERIFIED. A generated test or successful syntax check is not a bench pass.

Use drive D for project data. Canonical local repository is D:/UserData/ARIA/repo. Return evidence to the existing master; do not create another master/handoff.

Use concise prompts and outputs, bounded sessions and only necessary tools. Do not buy credits, enable paid overages, use separately billed API keys or launch repeated unattended work. Report budget/authentication failures clearly.
